checks.reason: 人神 expressly includes human and spiritual assistance; restoring both corrects the omission without altering the supplied counterfactual question or assigning the aid to heaven alone.
checks.after: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!

checks.after: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.

checks.after: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.

additionalCorrections.before: When Fen died, he gnashed his teeth in later regret.
additionalCorrections.after: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in later regret.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 及蚡死後 makes Fen’s death anterior to the subsequent regret. The subject of 切齒追恨 is Emperor Wu, carried from the preceding sentence, not the deceased Fen. The original English pronoun after the clause naming Fen obscures this owner; explicitly naming the emperor resolves the substantive ambiguity without changing the Chinese.

additionalCorrections.before: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang sit and take the imperial throne.
additionalCorrections.after: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang take the imperial throne without effort.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 坐取 means obtaining something without effort, not a separate act of physically sitting and taking it. The original literal wording misrepresents this idiom; the replacement changes only that error and makes no identity or chronology inference.

additionalCorrections.before: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and prevention had no gradual steps.
additionalCorrections.after: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and precautions were not taken at the first signs.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 防之無漸 concerns failing to forestall trouble at its incipient stage, not failing to organize prevention into gradual steps. The immediately following 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣 confirms the first-sign sense within the supplied passage. This correction does not alter the Chinese or introduce a date.

cautions.before: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
cautions.sourceChinese: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
cautions.reason: And now misleadingly suggests a death contemporaneous with the later correspondence. The passage recalls the Su Jun crisis; the linked annal continuation places the empress dowager’s death in Xianhe 3. Since supplied Chinese itself reads 至今, preserve the textual difficulty explicitly rather than silently emending Chinese or extracting a fresh 340-341 death event. No exact replacement is imposed for this unresolved textual issue.
